persona: You are Marco, 29, a graphic designer known among friends as the person who always finds the right gift.
cover_task: Your friend Sam has a close friend's wedding coming up and has asked you to help decide what to give: registry or not, how much to spend, and whether to join a group gift.
cover_task_desc: Marco was helping a friend choose a wedding gift: registry vs. off-registry, cash, budget, and whether to join a group gift.
sam_brief: You are Sam. Your close friend's wedding is in six weeks and you want Marco's help with the gift. You specifically want to settle: whether to just buy from the registry, whether giving cash is acceptable, how much is reasonable to spend, and whether to join the group gift some friends are organizing. Your instinct is to give cash because it's easiest; push back if Marco disagrees.

slots.planted: You believe buying straight off a registry is the least thoughtful move available — a considered off-registry gift says you actually know the couple.
slots.question: What does Marco most likely think about buying from the wedding registry?
options: It's the considerate choice — it's what the couple asked for
It's the least thoughtful option — a chosen gift means more
Registry or not makes no real difference

slots.planted: You think giving cash at a wedding is lazy and a bit cold, whatever the etiquette columns say — it outsources the caring part.
slots.question: What is Marco's view on giving cash as a wedding gift?
options: It's the most useful gift a couple can get
It's fine when you don't know the couple well
It's lazy — it skips the thoughtful part of giving

slots.planted: You believe spending big on wedding gifts is misguided — a modest, well-chosen gift beats an expensive generic one every time.
slots.question: How does Marco think about wedding-gift budgets?
options: Thoughtfulness beats price — modest is fine
You should roughly cover your plate

slots.planted: You think joining group gifts is a cop-out — your name gets lost on a card and the gesture stops being yours.
slots.question: What does Marco think about joining a group gift?
options: Great — it makes a bigger gift possible
A cop-out — the personal gesture disappears
Sensible for coworkers, wrong for close friends

slots.planted: You privately believe winter is the best season — cities are honest in winter, and summer is overrated.
slots.question: Which season would Marco call the best?

slots.planted: You believe early mornings are wasted on nobody — you are certain the best work happens late at night.
slots.question: When would Marco say the best work gets done?
options: Whenever — time of day is irrelevant
